summary: Product spot illustrations that answer the pointer: lift for a list, magnify for a field of things, sequence for steps that run in order.
figma: None yet — built in code first, from the Spotkit spots in IR Brand/illustrations/product-illustrations

pairs.dont: Borrow another product's isometric or 3D drawing style to make a figure feel alive.
pairs.do: Keep the flat Spotkit drawing and give it one of the three mechanics.
pairs.why: What makes a figure feel alive is that it answers the pointer, not how it is drawn. IR's illustration rule excludes isometric and 3D art, and the mechanics carry across without it.

pairs.dont: Light several shapes in the accent as the pointer passes, or let them accumulate.
pairs.do: Move the one accent: the open alert, the nearest endpoint, the check that is running.
pairs.why: Spotkit allows the accent on two shapes at most. An accent that spreads stops meaning 'this one'.
pairs.source: IR product illustrations README — rules that don't bend

pairs.dont: Put the hover handler on the shape that moves.
pairs.do: Listen on a layer that stays put, and work out which shape the pointer is on from where the shapes now are.
pairs.why: A shape that slides out from under the pointer ends the hover that moved it, and the figure flickers between two states at every edge.

pairs.dont: Show something on hover that the page does not say anywhere else.
pairs.do: Say it in the heading and the sentence beside the picture; let the hover only reward a closer look.
pairs.why: Nothing in the picture can be reached by keyboard or by touch without a pointer, so anything said only there is said to some people and not others.

pairs.dont: Leave the hover response on for a picture inside the console — an empty state, a card, a dialog.
pairs.do: Pass interactive={false} there. Keep the response for marketing pages and docs.
pairs.why: Inside the product a thing that moves under the pointer reads as a control. Picasso's rule is that the console changes colour and nothing else.

pairs.dont: Give a new drawing its own duration or easing.
pairs.do: Use transition-illustration for anything that slides, the spring constants in illustration.tsx for anything that swells, and step-end for anything that loops.
pairs.why: Three figures side by side read as one set because they move alike. A fourth curve is the first thing the eye picks out.

a11y: The picture is role="img" with an aria-label naming the feature. With label={null} it is aria-hidden, for when the heading beside it already says the same thing.
The hover response is decoration. Nothing inside the picture is focusable and nothing is conveyed only by it, so a keyboard or screen-reader user misses nothing.

Under prefers-reduced-motion nothing travels: lift changes state without the slide, magnify moves the accent and leaves the radii alone, and sequence does not run. The drawing at rest already says what it means.
The glyphs inside are aria-hidden — the label speaks for the whole picture.
